cards.text: Zophar the Naamathite just finished his speech: the triumph of the wicked is brief, and their joy doesn't last (Job 20:5). Now Job answers. And friend, after all the speeches he's been sitting through, I think Job's got a LOT to say.

cards.question: Job asks his friends to listen carefully to his words. He says that would be their ___ to him.

cards.text: Then Job adds a line with some bite: bear with him while he speaks, and after that, 'you may go on mocking.' That's the most polite 'let me finish, THEN you can roast me' in history.

cards.question: Job asks, 'Is my complaint against a man?' Then he asks why he should not be impatient.
Job wants his friends to take a real look at him. What does he tell them to do?

answers.text: Be appalled and cover their mouths
Be still and lift up their eyes
Be brave and take hold of his hand

cards.text: Then Job admits that when he remembers, terror takes hold and his body trembles in horror. And then he asks the big one.

cards.question: Zophar said the triumph of the wicked is brief. Job's big question is about the wicked too. What does he ask?

answers.text: Why do the wicked live on
Why do the wicked never rest
Why do the wicked fear death

cards.text: And they don't just live on. They grow old, they grow in power, and their descendants are established all around them, and Zophar said their joy was momentary while these folks are out here posing for family photos with EVERYBODY in them!

cards.question: Job says the homes of the wicked are safe from fear, with no rod of ___ from God upon them.

cards.text: Even their livestock is thriving: their bulls breed without fail, and their cows bear calves and don't miscarry. Friend, back in the Millers' kitchen I had more off days than these cows!

cards.question: Job paints a picture of the children of the wicked. What are they doing?

answers.text: Skipping about and singing to music
Working in the fields beside their fathers
Sitting quietly by the city gate

cards.question: Job says the wicked spend their days in prosperity, then go down to Sheol in terror.

cards.text: All that going for them, and here's what they tell God: 'Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.' I'm sorry... WHAT?

cards.question: The wicked also ask what they would gain if they pray to the Almighty.

cards.text: But Job is clear on one thing. The prosperity of the wicked is not in their own hands.

cards.question: Since the prosperity of the wicked isn't in their own hands, what does Job do with their counsel?

cards.text: Job keeps the questions coming: how often is the lamp of the wicked put out, and how often does disaster come on them, or God in His anger hand out destruction? HOW OFTEN? Somebody show Job the numbers!

cards.question: Job asks if the wicked really get swept away like something light in a storm. What picture does he use?

cards.text: Then Job brings up something people say. It is said that God lays up one's punishment for his children.

cards.question: People say God saves a man's punishment for his children. What does Job want instead?

answers.text: Let God repay the man himself
Let God forgive the whole family
Let the children be warned early

cards.text: Job wants the wicked man to see his own destruction and drink the wrath of the Almighty for himself. After all, once his months run out, what does he care about his household after him?

cards.question: Job asks if anyone can teach knowledge to God, since God judges even those on high.

cards.text: Then Job describes one man who dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease, his body well nourished. My edges went soft for YEARS before the drawer, and this guy's bones are rich with marrow right up to the end!

cards.question: Now Job describes another man. He dies in the ___ of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.
Of the two men Job describes, only the bitter one ends up lying in the dust with worms covering him.

cards.text: Then Job tells his friends he knows their thoughts, the schemes by which they would wrong him. He even says what they're thinking: 'Where now is the nobleman's house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?'

cards.question: Job's friends ask where the house of the wicked is now. Who does Job tell them to go ask?
Job says the evil man is ___ from the day of calamity and delivered from the day of wrath.

cards.text: Then Job asks who denounces the evil man's behavior to his face, and who repays him for what he has done. ...Crickets.

cards.question: When the evil man dies, how is he treated?

answers.text: He is carried to the grave and his tomb is watched
He is thrown outside the city and left unburied
He is buried in a hurry and quickly forgotten

cards.text: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number. Zophar said folks would ask, 'Where is he?' (Job 20:7), and Job's answer is: try the front of a VERY long line.

cards.question: Job calls his friends' comfort empty words, and says their answers remain full of ___.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch on the cooling rack for now. Trust me, friend, Job's story is far from over.

findings.problem: This true or false card restates verse 4 almost word for word, and the answer is True. No story card sets it up, because card 3 covers only verse 3. The baker has nothing to reason with, and the card doesn't ask anything about what the line means or why Job says it.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: The question says 'Zophar said the triumph of the wicked is brief.' That is Job 20:5, but the question gives no reference, and the card cites only Job 21:7.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card says 'Zophar said their joy was momentary.' That is Job 20:5, but there's no reference on this card, and the card cites only Job 21:7-8.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The joke places the wicked of Job 21 inside the modern comparison ('these folks are out here posing for family photos'). That blends the everyday image with the Bible setting. The card also packs the verse, the Zophar callback and the joke into one long run-on sentence, which is not short or punchy.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences: 'Job keeps the questions coming…', 'HOW OFTEN?' and 'Somebody show Job the numbers!'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card puts 'how often' in front of all three questions. In verse 17, only the lamp question has 'How often.' The other two are separate questions: 'Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question asks about being 'swept away like something light in a storm.' That rules out 'Leaves on a branch,' which isn't swept anywhere, and makes 'Straw before the wind' easy to spot.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This true or false card restates verse 22 with the answer True. The story card before it (verses 20-21) doesn't set it up, so the baker can't reason toward it. The card also doesn't ask what the line means.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card says 'God judges even those on high.' The text says 'since He judges those on high.' The word 'even' adds emphasis the text doesn't have.

'My edges went soft for YEARS before the drawer' adds a length of time to the backstory. The backstory says only that years of baking wore him down. It doesn't say how long his edges were soft before the drawer.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The card calls the quote 'what they're thinking.' The text introduces it with 'For you say,' so it is what they say.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke says the evil man is at 'the front of a VERY long line.' The verse just quoted says 'those before him are without number,' so the text shows he is not at the front.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The line that says the story isn't over nearly copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This last card is only the line that says the story isn't over. It tells no verse, but it cites Job 21:34, the verse card 16 already asked about.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the line that says the story isn't over, what should its "verses" field cite: the passage's last verse, nothing, or something else?
